title: Permission Without a Practitioner: Governance and Market Implications of the Additional Condition for Nonprescription Use
content: Background: In December 2024, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration finalized a rule permitting nonprescription marketing of a drug product with an additional condition for nonprescription use (ACNU), typically a sponsor-operated digital questionnaire, where labeling alone cannot ensure appropriate self-selection or actual use. The pathway has been discussed almost exclusively as a question of access. Methods: Document-based policy analysis of the final and proposed rules, the associated docket, prior agency actions on nonprescription classification, and the trial evidence for the leading candidate product, with forecasts stated as falsifiable propositions. Results: The condition generates identified clinical information held by a party that is neither a HIPAA covered entity nor subject to information-blocking requirements, and one purchase may generate records under three legal regimes. Because sponsors will accept self-reported inputs, the pathway will remain structurally unintegrable with the health record. The new postmarketing reporting category captures deviations from an approved process but not exclusion by an instrument operating as approved. Every payment mechanism cushioning the cost is tied to an insurance product, and payers may withdraw coverage of the prescription version after approval. Conclusions: Data protection, aggregate exclusion reporting, referral neutrality, and payment parity are more easily specified before the first approval than retrofitted afterward.
